items.exemplar:
A. At the 1787 Constitutional Convention, delegates clashed over representation: large states wanted proportional representation while small states demanded equality. The Great Compromise created a Senate with two senators per state and a House apportioned by population.

B. In 1798 Jefferson and Madison protested the Alien and Sedition Acts with the Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions, arguing that states could refuse to enforce federal laws they deemed unconstitutional.

C. President Jefferson justified the Louisiana Purchase on practical rather than strict-constructionist grounds, setting aside his constitutional doubts to double the nation's size.
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE example of debate over constitutional principles in the United States in the period 1787–1800.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of such debate in the same period.
C. Briefly explain ONE example of a political leader acting on constitutional principle in this period.
items.stimulus: Historian Joseph Ellis writes that the early republic was 'an extended argument about what the Revolution had actually meant' — with the Constitution's silences over federal versus state power guaranteeing that every crisis became a constitutional debate.
